title_en: Regulations on the Administration of Commercial Franchises

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated to regulate commercial franchise activities, promote the healthy and orderly development of commercial franchises, and maintain market order.
Article 2 Any person engaged in commercial franchise activities within the territory of the People's Republic of China shall comply with these Regulations.

Article 3 For the purposes of these Regulations, "commercial franchise" (hereinafter referred to as "franchise") means the business activity in which an enterprise (hereinafter referred to as the "franchisor") that owns business resources such as registered trademarks, enterprise logos, patents, and proprietary technologies licenses, in the form of a contract, the use of such business resources to another operator (hereinafter referred to as the "franchisee"), and the franchisee conducts business under a unified business model as agreed in the contract and pays franchise fees to the franchisor.
No entity or individual other than an enterprise shall act as a franchisor to engage in franchise activities.
Article 4 Engaging in franchise activities shall follow the principles of voluntary participation, fairness, and good faith.

Article 5 The commerce administration department of the State Council shall, in accordance with these Regulations, be responsible for supervising and administering franchise activities nationwide. The commerce administration departments of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and of the cities divided into districts, shall, in accordance with these Regulations, be responsible for supervising and administering franchise activities within their respective administrative regions.

Article 6 Any entity or individual shall have the right to report to the commerce administration department any act that violates these Regulations. Upon receiving a report, the commerce administration department shall promptly handle it according to law.

Article 7 A franchisor engaging in franchise activities shall possess a mature business model and have the capability to continuously provide the franchisee with services such as business guidance, technical support, and business training.
A franchisor engaging in franchise activities shall own at least two directly operated stores, each having been in operation for more than one year.

Article 9 The commerce administration department shall, within 10 days from the date of receiving the documents and materials submitted by the franchisor that comply with Article 8 of these Regulations, complete the record and notify the franchisor. If the documents and materials submitted by the franchisor are incomplete, the commerce administration department may require the franchisor to supplement them within 7 days.
Article 10 The commerce administration department shall publish the list of franchisors that have filed records on the government website and update it in a timely manner.

Article 12 The franchisor and the franchisee shall stipulate in the franchise contract that the franchisee may unilaterally dissolve the contract within a certain period after the conclusion of the franchise contract.

Article 13 The franchise term stipulated in the franchise contract shall be no less than three years, unless otherwise agreed by the franchisee.
Where the franchisor and the franchisee renew the franchise contract, the preceding paragraph shall not apply.

Article 14 The franchisor shall provide the franchisee with the franchise operation manual and continuously provide the franchisee with services such as business guidance, technical support, and business training in accordance with the agreed content and methods.
Article 15 The quality and standards of franchised products or services shall comply with the requirements of laws, administrative regulations, and relevant state provisions.

Article 16 If the franchisor requires the franchisee to pay fees before concluding the franchise contract, the franchisor shall, in writing, explain to the franchisee the purpose of such fees and the conditions and methods for their refund.

Article 17 Promotion and advertising fees collected by the franchisor from the franchisee shall be used for the purposes agreed in the contract. The use of such fees shall be disclosed to the franchisee in a timely manner.
In promotion and advertising activities, the franchisor shall not engage in deceptive or misleading conduct, and the advertisements published by the franchisor shall not contain content promoting the income of the franchisee from engaging in franchise activities.

Article 18 Without the consent of the franchisor, the franchisee shall not transfer the franchise rights to others.
The franchisee shall not disclose or allow others to use the trade secrets of the franchisor that the franchisee possesses.
Article 19 The franchisor shall, in the first quarter of each year, report to the commerce administration department on the franchise contracts concluded in the previous year.
Article 20 The franchisor shall, in accordance with the provisions of the commerce administration department of the State Council, establish and implement a complete information disclosure system.

Article 21 A franchisor shall, at least 30 days prior to the conclusion of a franchise contract, provide the franchisee in writing with the information prescribed in Article 22 of these Regulations, and provide the text of the franchise contract.

Article 23 The information provided by a franchisor to a franchisee shall be true, accurate and complete, and the franchisor shall not conceal any relevant information or provide false information.
If any major change occurs in the information provided by a franchisor to a franchisee, the franchisor shall promptly notify the franchisee.
If a franchisor conceals any relevant information or provides false information, the franchisee may dissolve the franchise contract.

Article 24 If a franchisor engages in franchise activities without meeting the conditions prescribed in Article 7, paragraph 2 of these Regulations, the competent commerce department shall order it to make corrections, confiscate its illegal gains, impose a fine of not less than RMB 100,000 yuan but not more than RMB 500,000 yuan, and make a public announcement.
If any entity or individual other than an enterprise engages in franchise activities as a franchisor, the competent commerce department shall order it to cease the illegal business activities, confiscate its illegal gains, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than RMB 100,000 yuan but not more than RMB 500,000 yuan.

Article 25 If a franchisor fails to file for the record with the competent commerce department in accordance with Article 8 of these Regulations, the competent commerce department shall order it to file within a time limit and impose a fine of not less than RMB 10,000 yuan but not more than RMB 50,000 yuan; if it still fails to file after the expiration of the time limit, the competent commerce department shall impose a fine of not less than RMB 50,000 yuan but not more than RMB 100,000 yuan, and make a public announcement.

Article 26 If a franchisor violates the provisions of Article 16 or Article 19 of these Regulations, the competent commerce department shall order it to make corrections, and may impose a fine of not more than RMB 10,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, it shall impose a fine of not less than RMB 10,000 yuan but not more than RMB 50,000 yuan, and make a public announcement.

Article 27 If a franchisor violates the provisions of Article 17, paragraph 2 of these Regulations, the administrative department for industry and commerce shall order it to make corrections, and impose a fine of not less than RMB 30,000 yuan but not more than RMB 100,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, it shall impose a fine of not less than RMB 100,000 yuan but not more than RMB 300,000 yuan, and make a public announcement; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
If a franchisor uses advertising to commit acts of deception or misleading, it shall be punished in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Advertising Law.

Article 28 If a franchisor violates the provisions of Article 21 or Article 23 of these Regulations, and the franchisee reports to the competent commerce department and the report is verified, the competent commerce department shall order it to make corrections, and impose a fine of not less than RMB 10,000 yuan but not more than RMB 50,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, it shall impose a fine of not less than RMB 50,000 yuan but not more than RMB 100,000 yuan, and make a public announcement.

Article 29 Where property of others is defrauded under the guise of franchise, if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if it does not constitute a crime, the public security organ shall impose a penalty in accordance with the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Public Security Administration Punishments.
Where pyramid selling activities are engaged in under the guise of franchise, a penalty shall be imposed in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Regulations on Prohibition of Pyramid Selling.

Article 30 If a staff member of the competent commerce department abuses his/her powers, neglects his/her duties, or engages in malpractice for personal gain, if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if it does not constitute a crime, he/she shall be given a sanction according to law.

Article 31 Where trademark licensing or patent licensing is involved in franchise activities, it shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the relevant laws and administrative regulations on trademarks and patents.

Article 32 Relevant trade associations, under the guidance of the competent department of commerce under the State Council, shall formulate norms for franchise activities in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations, strengthen industry self-discipline, and provide relevant services to the parties to franchise activities.

Article 33 A franchisor that has already engaged in franchise activities prior to the coming into force of these Regulations shall, within one year from the date of coming into force of these Regulations, file for the record with the competent commerce department in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations; if it fails to file within the time limit, it shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of Article 25 of these Regulations.
The franchisor prescribed in the preceding paragraph shall not be subject to the provisions of Article 7, paragraph 2 of these Regulations.
Article 34 These Regulations shall come into force as of May 1, 2007.
